- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >35.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct; apply a “cool-down” penalty: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — forecast tends to revert to prior 10-day average; use that as anchor for correction.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model underestimates long-term (15–30 day) trends; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for days 15–30 if no recent volatility.
- If true outcome shows sudden upward movement (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model fails to anticipate; apply “volatility lag” rule: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and scale up by 1–2%.
- Model underestimates late-period (days 25–30) outcomes when true values are rising; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for final 5 days if prior 5 days show upward momentum.
